name: Web Security
description: Defending web applications against common exploits, injection vulnerabilities, and authentication flaws.

topics.title: SQL Injection (SQLi)
topics.notes: Covers how unvalidated user inputs allow attackers to interfere with backend database queries. Explains parameterized queries as the primary defense.
topics.why_it_matters: SQL injection remains one of the most critical web application vulnerabilities, leading to severe data breaches if left unmitigated.

topics.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS)
topics.notes: Details Stored, Reflected, and DOM-based XSS vulnerabilities. Explores Content Security Policy (CSP) and context-aware HTML output encoding.
topics.why_it_matters: XSS allows malicious scripts to run in victims' browsers, compromising cookies, session tokens, and sensitive client data.

topics.title: Cross-Site Request Forgery (CSRF)
topics.notes: Explains how unauthorized commands are transmitted from a trusted user. Discusses anti-CSRF tokens and SameSite cookie attributes.
topics.why_it_matters: CSRF exploits ambient credentials (like cookies), forcing authenticated users to unintentionally perform sensitive actions.

topics.title: CORS & Browser Origin Security
topics.notes: Comprehensive breakdown of Same-Origin Policy (SOP), preflight OPTIONS requests, and proper Access-Control header configurations.
topics.why_it_matters: Misconfigured CORS headers can inadvertently expose private APIs to malicious third-party origins.
